decision.reason: The state-only body is only the marker (12 estimated tokens in every failure); the rationale is the excess. The model call was necessary to know whether the rationale would fit, and a shorter rationale could have committed. A pre-call guard would therefore convert one refusal into another, not prevent a doomed transaction.

retryEvidence.reason: The retries are not uniformly futile. In T9-s1-E1-r2 and T10-s1-E1-r1 the first attempt failed on a 200-token span, and the next attempt committed after folding a ~9.2k-token span. A blanket retry suppression would lose those two commits. A refusal cache keyed on the exact span seqs is a candidate, but the archive does not retain the failed attempts' span seqs, so its effect on these cells is unverified. It belongs to a future round whose witness captures those seqs.

decision.admissionMismatch: admitLeafEconomically prices the widest legal span with retainTokens=0, while the executor folds the span left after spec.retainTokens. In these cells the executed span is 58-207 tokens, below the 530-token framing fallback, but that does not prove the decider would have refused it. Whether economic admission prevents these attempts needs a dedicated replay with the real measurement; it is a hypothesis, not a result.
decision.next: Pre-register the shipped tier configuration and a zero-request preflight that checks the EXECUTED fold span, not only the widest legal span. Capture the selected span seqs in the witness so a future round can test a same-span refusal cache. Do not lower the rationale budget or tune the prompt.
